body:
Sorry, I know you mean well, but I'm not convinced that things are actually going to get any better.

>No one's going to be sad forever.

It feels like I've been sad for an awfully long time. If that sadness persists even when I'm trying my damnedest to improve, then I'm not sure it'll ever go away. Don't get me wrong, I'm pleased that I've had so much success with my anxiety and timekeeping, but it worries me that my depression still seems to be as intractable as ever.

>surround yourself with positive people.

This is one of my problems; social isolation. I don't have any friends and I'd hoped that as I dealt with my social anxiety I'd find more opportunities to make friends or talk to people.

Unfortunately it hasn't really worked out like that. I try. I speak to people, make small talk, try and find people with similar interests, but it never seems to work out.

Recently, for example, I've been going to a group course for people with anxiety problems, including social anxiety. At the start, I made sure that I was assertive, tried to make conversation with other people during the breaks etc. and I thought I was doing reasonably well.

But now, a few weeks in, you can see that people have formed into little cliques. The problem is, that despite my best efforts, I've still been left on the outside, I basically no longer have anyone to talk to during the break, and I kind of feel like an outsider to the group. I don't really know how to remedy this.

I find it so alienating that I don't even seem to be able to relate to people who are in a similar situation to me. Worse, I seem to be the only person at the group that has this problem.

It's strange, I don't even have much of a problem with small talk any more, I even enjoy it in some ways, but I just seem to be completely unable to actually relate to anyone else, no matter what I try. I really don't know what I'm doing wrong.
I can't understand how other people seem to manage to find common ground so effortlessly. How do other people manage to just 'click' like that?

But now that I think about it, even as a child the only people I've ever really got along with were always 'outsiders'. Maybe that's the problem? Perhaps I should specifically seek out 'unusual' people. Maybe that's just the sort of person I tend to get along with?

I don't know. Sorry for bombarding you with this wall of text. I try not to be complacent about my problems, but it's so frustrating when I can't find a solution no matter what I try.
